newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia Treasury pleased with tender result.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia Treasury pleased with tender result.

text.p: The Australian Treasury was "very pleased" with the response to its first offering of the August 2020 indexed bonds, and is pleased with the way the indexed bond market is developing, a Treasury official said on Thursday.
"We are very pleased with the result, very pleased with the launch of the new line," the official said, soon after the results of the A$250 million tender were released.

The tender, conducted by the Reserve Bank of Australia, went off at a weighted average of 4.586 percent. A total of A$251 million was issued to the public, with accepted yields ranging from 4.54 to 4.61 percent.
In addition, the Reserve Bank took up A$20 million of the issue for its own portfolio, for which it will pay a price based on the weighted average yield.

"We think that particularly given the larger than normal tender size, which is aimed at quickly building up liquidity, and the usual pricing uncertainty that's associated with any new line, that it was quite a successful tender," the official said.
Indexed bond tenders are normally around A$100 million.
The tender brings to five the number of indexed bond series, with the other maturies being in 1998, 2005, 2010 and 2015.
All issues mature in August, and all carry a 4.0 percent annual coupon, paid quarterly.
Indexed bonds are bonds where the nominal value of the bond is adjusted each quarter by the change in the consumer price index, with the quarterly interest paid on the adjusted capital value.

Treasury said that while building up the new issue was a priority, they still had the option of adding to the 2015 issue. Changes in taxation laws a few years ago had meant that the other lines would not be added to, Treasury said.
"I think it would be fair to say we'll be looking to further build liquidity in this new line sooner rather than later as a priority," the official said.
"So probably the issuance of the 2020's will probably tend to dominate the next few tenders. But we've certainly still got option of issuing the 2015's as well."
In the budget, an indicative issuance project for indexed bonds of A$500 to A$1 billion for the 1996/97 year to June 30 was announced.
The official also said that Treasury had been pleased with the development of the indexed bond market over recent years, not just in Commonwealth indexed bonds but also infrastructure related issues.
"It still has its challenges I think but we have been pleased to see that the market at large has been developing and we hope that this will be another step in that direction," the official said.
